# Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal

## This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 52

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 52] Contents of this Practice Direction

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 52] SECTION VII – BUNDLES, AMENDMENT AND SKELETON ARGUMENTS

## Contents of this Practice Direction

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] This Practice Direction is divided into the following sections –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section I – Introduction and interpretation

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section II – Starting an appeal to the Court of Appeal, Grounds of Appeal and Skeleton Arguments

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section III –Respondent’s notice and respondent’s skeleton argument

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section IV – Procedure where permission to appeal is sought from the Court of Appeal

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section V –Timetable

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section VI – Management of the appeal

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section VII – Bundles, amendment and supplementary skeleton arguments

## SECTION I – INTRODUCTION AND INTERPRETATION

## 1. In this Practice Direction –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] ‘appeal notice’ means either an appellant’s notice in form N161 or a respondent’s notice in form N162 ;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] ‘appellant’s notice’ means an appeal notice filed by an appellant and a ‘respondent’s notice’ means an appeal notice filed by a respondent;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] ‘hearing date’ means the date on which the appeal is listed to be heard, including a‘floating’ date over two or more days;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] ‘listing window notification’ means the letter sent by the Civil Appeals Office in accordance with Section 5: Timetable Part 1 notifying the parties of the window within which the appeal is likely to be heard; and ‘date of the listing window notification’ means the date of such letter;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] ‘replacement skeleton argument’ means a skeleton argument which has been amended in order to include cross references to the appeal bundle and is lodged and served in accordance with the timetable at Section 5 Part 2. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 1. In this Practice Direction –] 2. The court may make such directions as the case may require and such directions will prevail over any provision of this practice direction. ## SECTION II – STARTING AN APPEAL TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Filing the appellant’s notice and accompanying documents

## 3. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (1) An appellant’s notice (Form N161), including grounds of appeal on a separate sheet, must be filed and served in all cases. The appellant’s notice must be accompanied by the appropriate fee or, if appropriate, a fee remission certificate. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (2) If the appellant is legally represented, the appellant’s notice and accompanying documents must be filed using the HMCTS e-filing service. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (3) If the appellant is not legally represented, the appellant’s notice and accompanying documents must be filed using the HMCTS e-filing service by e-mail, or by post to the Civil Appeals Office Registry, Room E307, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London, WC2A 2LL. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (4) At the same time as filing an appellant’s notice, the appellant must provide for the use of the court one copy of each of the following –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (a) the sealed order or other determination being appealed;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (b) any order granting or refusing permission to appeal, together with a copy of the judge’s or tribunal’s reasons for granting or refusing permission to appeal;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (c) any witness statements or affidavits relied on in support of any application included in the appellant’s notice;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (d) in cases where the decision of the lower court was itself made on appeal, the first order, the reasons given by the judge who made it, and the appellant’s notice of appeal against that order;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (e) in a claim for judicial review or a statutory appeal, the original decision which was the subject of the application to the lower court;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (f) omitted;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (g) the appellant’s skeleton argument in support of the appeal;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (h) the approved transcript of the judgment. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (5) Where the appellant applies for permission to appeal, additional documents are required: see Section 4 of this Practice Direction. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 3.] (6) Provisions in relation to the skeleton argument are set out in paragraph 31. ## Extension of time for filing appellant’s notice

## 4. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (1) Where the time for filing an appellant’s notice has expired, the appellant must –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (a) file the appellant’s notice; and

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (b) include in that appellant’s notice an application for an extension of time. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (2) The appellant’s notice must state the reason for the delay and the steps taken prior to the application being made. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (3) Where the appellant’s notice includes an application for an extension of time and permission to appeal has been given or is not required, the respondent has the right to oppose that application and to be heard at any hearing of that application. In respect of any application to extend time –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (a) The respondent must–

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (i) be served with a copy of any evidence filed in support of the application; and

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (ii) inform the court in writing of any objections to the grant of the extension of time within 7 days of being served with the appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (b) A respondent who unreasonably opposes an application for an extension of time may be ordered to pay the costs of the application. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 4.] (c) An application for an extension of time will normally be determined without a hearing unless the court directs otherwise. ## Grounds of appeal

## 5. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5.] (1) The grounds of appeal must identify as concisely as possible the respects in which the judgment of the court below is –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5.] (a) wrong; or

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5.] (b) unjust because of a serious procedural or other irregularity,

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5.] as required by rule 52.21(3). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5.] (2) The reasons why the decision under appeal is wrong or unjust must not be included in the grounds of appeal and must be confined to the skeleton argument. ## Second appeals

## 5A An application to make a second appeal must identify in the grounds of appeal –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5A An application to make a second appeal must identify in the grounds of appeal –] (1) the important point of principle or practice, or

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5A An application to make a second appeal must identify in the grounds of appeal –] (2) the compelling reason

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 5A An application to make a second appeal must identify in the grounds of appeal –] which is said to justify the grant of permission to appeal. ## Non-availability of documents

## 6

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 6] (1) If the appellant is unable to provide any of the necessary documents in time, the appellant must complete the appeal notice on the basis of the available documents. The notice may be amended subsequently with the permission of the court (see paragraph 30). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 6] (2) Any application for a transcript at public expense should be made within the appellant’s notice. ## Service on the respondent

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Service on the respondent] 7.1 The Civil Appeals Office will not serve documents. Where service is required by the Rules or this Practice Direction, it must be effected by the parties. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Service on the respondent] 7.1A The appellant’s skeleton argument in respect of an application for permission to appeal must be served on each respondent at the same time as service of the appellant’s notice,or at the same time as it is filed with the Court, if later. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Service on the respondent] 7.2 The evidence in support of any application made in an appellant’s notice must be filed and served with the appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Service on the respondent] 7.3 An application for an order to dispense with service of the appellant’s notice under rule 6.28 must be made in the appeal notice or, thereafter, by application notice under Part 23. ## SECTION III – RESPONDENT’S NOTICE (RULE 52.13) AND RESPONDENT’S SKELETON ARGUMENT

## Respondent’s notice

## 8. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 8.] (1) A respondent who seeks to appeal against any part of the order made by the court below must file an appeal notice. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 8.] (2) A respondent who seeks a variation of the order of the lower court must file an appeal notice and must obtain permission to appeal. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 8.] (3) A respondent who seeks to contend that the order of the court below should be upheld for reasons other than those given by that court must file a respondent’s notice. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 8.] (4) The notice may be amended subsequently with the permission of the court (see paragraph 30). ## Skeleton argument to be lodged with the respondent’s notice

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Skeleton argument to be lodged with the respondent’s notice] 9. A respondent who files a respondent’s notice must, within 14 days of filing the notice, lodge a skeleton argument with the court and serve a copy of the skeleton argument on every other party to the appeal. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Skeleton argument to be lodged with the respondent’s notice] (Provisions in relation to the skeleton argument are set out in paragraph 31.)

## 10. Omitted

## Applications within respondent’s notice

## 11. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 11.] (1) A respondent may include an application within a respondent’s notice. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 11.] (2) The parties must consider whether it would be more convenient for any application to be listed with the appeal or whether the application needs to be considered in advance. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 11.] (3) Where parties consider that the time estimate for the appeal will be affected by listing the application with the appeal, they must inform the court without delay. ## Time limits: rule 52.13(4) and (5)

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Time limits: rule 52.13(4) and (5)] 12. Where an extension of time is required, the respondent must apply in the respondent’s notice and explain the delay. ## Respondent’s skeleton argument (where no respondent’s notice filed)

## 13. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 13.] (1) In all cases where the respondent is legally represented and proposes to address the court, the respondent must lodge and serve a skeleton argument. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 13.] (2) A respondent’s skeleton argument must be lodged and served in accordance with Part 1 of the Timetable in Section 5. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 13.] (Provisions in relation to the skeleton argument are set out in paragraph 31.)

## SECTION IV – PROCEDURE WHERE PERMISSION TO APPEAL IS SOUGHT FROM THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Documents for use on an application for permission

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Documents for use on an application for permission] 14. Within 14 days of  the appeal notice being sealed by the court, the appellant must lodge a core bundle (and, if necessary, a supplementary bundle) for the application for permission to appeal, prepared in accordance with paragraph 27. ## Determination of applications for permission to appeal

## 15. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 15.] (1) Applications for permission to appeal will be determined by the court without a hearing unless the judge considering the application directs that the application be determined at an oral hearing in accordance with rule 52.5(2). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 15.] (2) If a judge directs that an oral hearing should take place, the hearing will be listed before the same judge no later than 14 days after the direction was given, unless the court directs otherwise. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 15.] (3) When directing that an oral hearing should take place, the judge may also identify any issue or issues on which the applicant should specifically focus its submissions at the oral hearing in order to assist the court to determine the application and may direct the respondent to file and serve written submissions and to attend the oral hearing. ## Permission hearing

## 16. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 16.] (1) The court will notify the respondent of any oral hearing but the respondent is not expected to attend unless the court so directs. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 16.] (2) If the court directs the respondent to attend the permission hearing, the appellant must supply the respondent with a copy of the skeleton argument and any documents to which the appellant intends to refer. ## 17. Omitted

## Limited permission: rule 52.6(2)

## 18. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 18.] (1) If, under rule 52.6(2), the court grants permission to appeal on some issues only, it will –

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 18.] (a) refuse permission on any remaining issues; or

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 18.] (b) adjourn the application in respect of those issues to the hearing of the appeal. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 18.] (2) If the court adjourns the application under sub-paragraph (1)(b), the appellant must inform the court and the respondent in writing, within 14 days after the date of the court’s order, whether the appellant intends to pursue the application. If the appellant intends to pursue the application, the parties must include in any time estimate for the appeal hearing an allowance for the adjourned application. ## Respondents actions when served with the appellant’s notice

## 19. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (1)

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (a) If the appellant seeks permission to appeal a respondent is permitted, and is encouraged, within 14 days of service of the appellant’s notice or skeleton argument if later to file and serve upon the appellant and any other respondent a brief statement of any reasons why permission should be refused, in whole or in part. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (b) The statement should be not more than 3 pages long, and should be directed to the relevant threshold test for the grant of permission to appeal. The statement must also comply with paragraph 31(1)(b). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (c) The statement should identify issues to which the appeal should be limited, and any conditions to which the appeal should be subject (see Rule 52.6(2)). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (2)

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (a) If the appellant makes any application in addition to an application for permission to appeal (such as a stay of execution, an injunction pending appeal or an extension of time for appeal) a respondent should include in its written statement under paragraph 19(1)(a) any reasons why that application should be refused or granted only on terms. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (b) If, exceptionally, a respondent wishes to rely upon evidence for that purpose its evidence should be included in its written statement, supported by a statement of truth, or filed and served upon the appellant and any other respondent at the same time as its written statement under paragraph 19(1)(a). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 19.] (3) Unless the court directs otherwise, a respondent need take no further steps when served with an appellant’s notice prior to being notified that permission to appeal has been granted. ## Respondent’s costs of permission applications

## 20. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 20.] (1) There will normally be no order for the recovery of the costs of a respondent’s written statement. In most cases an application for permission to appeal will be determined without the need for the respondent to attend a hearing. In such circumstances an order for costs will not normally be made in favour of a respondent who voluntarily attends a hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 20.] (2) If the court directs the respondent to file submissions or attend a hearing, it will normally award costs to the respondent if permission is refused. ## SECTION V – TIMETABLE

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > SECTION V – TIMETABLE] 21. Subject to any specific directions that may be given by the court, the timetable for the conduct of an appeal after the date of the listing window notification is set out below:

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > SECTION V – TIMETABLE] Timetable Part 1 – Listing window notification to lodging bundle

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > SECTION V – TIMETABLE] the appellant’s notice if permission has been given by the lower court or is not needed;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > SECTION V – TIMETABLE] notification that permission has been granted by the Court of Appeal; or

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > SECTION V – TIMETABLE] notification that the permission application will be listed with the appeal to follow

## Paragraph 13 (respondent’s skeleton argument where no Respondent’s Notice filed)

## Paragraph 31 (skeleton argument)

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Paragraph 31 (skeleton argument)] Timetable Part 2 – Steps to be taken once hearing date fixed: lodging bundles, supplemental skeletons and bundles of authorities

## SECTION VI – MANAGEMENT OF THE APPEAL

## Listing and hear-by dates

## 22. The hear-by date is the last day of the listing window. ## Appeal Questionnaire

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Appeal Questionnaire] 23. The appellant must complete and file the Appeal Questionnaire and serve it on the respondent within 14 days after the date of the listing window notification. ## Time estimates

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Time estimates] 24. If the respondent disagrees with the appellant’s time estimate, the respondent must inform the court within 7 days of service of the Appeal Questionnaire. In the absence of such notification the respondent will be deemed to have accepted the appellant’s time estimate. ## Multiple appeals

## 25. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 25.] (1) If two or more appeals are pending in the same or related proceedings, the parties must seek directions as to whether they should be heard together or consecutively by the same judges. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 25.] (2) Whether appeals are heard together or consecutively, the parties must attempt to agree a single appeal bundle or set of bundles for all the appeals and seek directions if they are unable to do so. ## Expedition

## 26. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26.] (1) The court may direct that the hearing of an appeal be expedited. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26.] (2) The court will deal with requests for expedition without a hearing. Requests for expedition must be made by letter setting out succinctly the grounds on which expedition is sought. The letter (or, if time is particularly short, email) must be marked for the immediate attention of the court and copied to the other parties to the appeal. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26.] (3) If an expedited appeal hearing is required as a matter of extreme urgency, the Civil Appeals Office must be informed as soon as possible. If necessary, parties or their legal representatives should call the Royal Courts of Justice switchboard on 020 7947 6000 and ask a member of the security staff to contact the Duty Judge. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26.] (4) An expedited hearing will be listed at the convenience of the court and not according to the availability of counsel. ## Nautical Assessors Assisting in the Court of Appeal from Decisions of the Admiralty Court

## 26B. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26B.] (1) Where there is an appeal from the Admiralty Court in a collision claim or other claim involving issues of navigation or seamanship, the Court of Appeal will, unless the court otherwise orders, be assisted by two nautical assessors. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26B.] (2) The nautical assessors will consist of one Elder Brother of Trinity House (nominated by Trinity House but appointed by the Master of the Rolls or a court officer) and one member of the Honourable Company of Master Mariners (nominated by the Honourable Company but appointed by the Master of the Rolls or a court officer). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26B.] (3) If either party in any appeal seeks a different order from the above they should apply to the Court of Appeal at the time when the notice of appeal or respondent’s notice is served. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26B.] (4) In the absence of any such application by the parties, the Master of the Rolls or a court officer may also decide that a different order is appropriate having regard to the particular circumstances of the case. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > 26B.] (5) In this paragraph, “court officer” means a court officer assigned to the Civil Appeals Office authorised to exercise the jurisdiction of the Court of Appeal under rule 52.24.”. ## SECTION VII – BUNDLES, AMENDMENT AND SKELETON ARGUMENTS

## Bundle of documents

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] 27. This paragraph of the Practice Direction should be read in conjunction with the Timetable in paragraph 21 above. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (1) Core bundle for permission to appeal: Subject to any direction made by the court, the applicant must lodge a core bundle containing only those documents listed in the relevant core bundle index accessible on the Court of Appeal (Civil Division) section of the Justice website (at http://hmctsformfinder.justice.gov.uk/HMCTS/GetForms.do?court_forms_category=Court%20of%20Appeal%20Civil%20Division ) or available from the Civil Appeals Office. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (2) Supplementary bundle for permission to appeal: For an application for permission to appeal any additional documents may be included in a supplementary bundle, but only where they are relevant to the grounds of appeal and where it will be necessary for the court to read the document for the purposes of determining whether to grant permission to appeal and any related application. The following documents may be considered for inclusion in a supplementary bundle:

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (a) statements of case;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (b) application notices;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (c) other orders made in the case;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (d) witness statements made in support of any application made in the appellant’s notice;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (e) other witness statements relevant to the issues raised in the grounds of appeal;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (f) key contemporaneous documents. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (3) Service of indexes for the permission to appeal bundles: The applicant for permission to appeal must serve on every respondent a copy of the index for the core bundle for permission to appeal and a copy of the index for any supplementary bundle for permission to appeal at the same time as the bundles are lodged with the court (i.e. within 14 days of the appeal notice: paragraph 14 above). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (4) Respondent’s statement for permission to appeal: In accordance with paragraph 19, a respondent is encouraged to file and serve a respondent’s statement in response to an application for permission to appeal. Any respondent’s statement will be copied to the core bundle by the Civil Appeals Office. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (5) Respondent’s Notice: A respondent who wishes to file a respondent’s notice must do so in accordance with the time limits in CPR Part 52.13. If the respondent seeks permission to appeal in their respondent’s notice they must on the date when the respondent’s skeleton argument is due to be filed lodge a respondent’s supplementary permission to appeal bundle. That bundle must contain any documents not included in the appellant’s bundle(s) for permission to appeal which are necessary for the court to read for the purpose of determining whether to grant the respondent permission to appeal, including the respondent’s notice and the respondent’s skeleton argument. On the same date the respondent must serve on every other party a copy of the index for that bundle. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (6) Reviewing the case after the grant of permission to appeal: Promptly after permission to appeal is granted to any party and before the appeal skeleton arguments are due to be filed under the Timetable, the parties must review the case with a view to resolution or refinement of the issues to be determined at the appeal hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (7) Bundles for the appeal hearing: Subject to any direction made by the court, the appellant must not less than 42 days before the date for the appeal hearing file and serve a core bundle for the appeal hearing and (if required) a supplementary bundle for the appeal hearing. The appellant must seek to agree the contents of the core bundle and the supplementary bundle for the appeal hearing with all other parties in accordance with sub-paragraphs (8) and (9) below. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (8) Core bundle for the appeal hearing

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (a) In accordance with the Timetable the appellant must serve on every respondent a proposed bundle index for the core bundle for the appeal hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (b) The respondent must either agree the proposed bundle index for the core bundle or notify the appellant of the documents that the respondent considers should be included in, or removed from, the core bundle by sending a revised index. The appellant and respondent must seek to agree the contents of the core bundle. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (c) The core bundle must be lodged by the appellant in accordance with the Timetable and must contain the final form of the skeleton arguments to be relied upon at the hearing, cross-referenced to the pagination in the bundles for the appeal hearing (i.e. the replacement skeleton arguments). [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (d) The core bundle for the appeal hearing must contain only those documents required in the core bundle for permission to appeal, together with copies of the following documents:

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (i) any respondent’s notice;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (ii) the appellant’s replacement skeleton argument (see paragraph 1 above for definition);

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (iii) the respondent’s replacement skeleton argument(see paragraph 1 above for definition);

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (iv) a copy of any orders made in the Court of Appeal;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (v) if permission to appeal was granted at an oral hearing, a transcript of the judgment giving permission to appeal. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (9) Supplementary bundle for the appeal hearing:

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (a) In accordance with the Timetable the appellant must serve on every respondent a proposed bundle index for the supplementary bundle for the appeal hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (b) The respondent must either agree the proposed bundle index for the supplementary bundle or notify the appellant of the documents that the respondent considers should be included in, or removed from, the supplementary bundle by sending a revised index. The appellant and respondent must seek to agree the contents of the supplementary bundle. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (c) The supplementary bundle may only contain documents relevant to the grounds of appeal which it will be necessary for the court to read in preparation for or during the appeal hearing. Where a party is represented,this must be certified by the advocate responsible for arguing the case. The following documents may be considered for inclusion in the supplementary bundle:

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (i) statements of case;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (ii) application notices;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (iii) other orders made in the case;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (iv) witness statements relevant to the issues raised in the grounds of appeal;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (v) key contemporaneous documents. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (10) Reviewing the case before the appeal hearing: After the appeal skeleton arguments are filed and served, and in accordance with the Timetable, the parties must review the case with a view to resolution or refinement of the issues to be determined at the appeal hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (11) Size of supplementary bundle: No supplementary bundle (whether for permission to appeal or for an appeal hearing) may exceed one lever arch file of 350 pages in size, unless the court gives permission. An application for permission to file a supplementary bundle of more than 350 pages must be made by application notice in accordance with CPR Part 23 and specify exactly what additional documents the party wishes to include; why it is necessary to put the additional documents before the court; and whether there is agreement between the parties as to their inclusion. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (12) Unagreed documents bundles for the appeal hearing: If there is no agreement in relation to inclusion of a particular document in the bundles for the appeal hearing, it must be placed in a separate unagreed documents bundle prepared by the party who has proposed its inclusion, and the bundle clearly labelled as such. The permission of the court is required to rely on an unagreed documents bundle. An application for permission must be made by application notice in accordance with CPR Part 23 and include a short statement of not more than three 20 A4 pages explaining why the unagreed documents are relevant and why it is necessary to put them before the court. Any unagreed documents bundle, including at the front the application notice and supporting statement, must be filed and served not less than 42 days before the date for the appeal hearing. Unless the court directs otherwise, the application will be determined by the court at the appeal hearing. [Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (13) Bundle format: Core, supplementary and unagreed documents bundles must—

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (a) be bound and any ring binder folder must be in fully working order;

[Practice Direction 52C – appeals to the court of appeal > Bundle of documents] (b) be paginated.
